newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Banks buoy Brussels bourse, but future uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Banks buoy Brussels bourse, but future uncertain.

text.p: Booming Belgian banking stocks buoyed the Brussels bourse on Monday, but traders said the future was uncertain due to volatility on the U.S. market and with a shortened trading week in Europe in prospect.

"This market is very vulnerable to events in the United States. But what happens there is quite unpredictable," one trader said. "So the chances are we will range-trade even though European fundamentals are good."
The Bel-20 blue chip index ended a thinly-traded day up 0.68 percent at 2,217.16.
Only 1.7 billion francs of Belgian shares changed hands, well below the average daily volume.
Traders said the lack of trade accentuated today's price rise, with the index climbing over one percent at one stage.

They noted that volatility would be aggravated by the one-day May Day holiday on Thursday and the likelihood that many traders will also take Friday off to create a four-day weekend despite the fact that officially markets are open.
Traders said the main feature of Monday's market was the strength of stocks in the financial sector.
BBL ended 2.4 percent up at 8,640 francs, with Generale Bank up 1.3 percent at 3,120 francs and Kredietbank up 1.9 percent at 13,575 francs.
Traders said the rise was partly speculative, partly due to the dollar and partly a recovery after stocks recently lagged the wider market.
Non-ferrous metals firm Union Miniere had a good day, rising at one stage to 2,980 francs before settling for a 0.5 percent increase at 2,925 francs.
Traders said the rise was in part due to the dollar's strength and in part to a report that LME zinc stocks fell.
Chemicals and drugs firm UCB took heart from the stronger dollar, up 1.0 percent at 98,000 francs, as did steel cord and wire maker Bekaert, up 0.6 percent at 22,500.
Traders said Bekaert remained a good cyclical stock and was attracting investors.
Retailer Colruyt rose 0.5 percent to 14,725 francs after news last week it gained market share in Belgium in 1996 and on a reassessment of the stock which has lagged the market this year.
